catalog_quote: II Initial main stress, no info on sec stress: ... Ngarluma (T76): Inferred from: O'Grady, Geoffrey N. (1957). Fieldnotes. Ms, AIATSIS, Canberra. [Appendix D preamble, p.235] This is a list of languages categorised by stress type and annotated with the main descriptive source and some codes denoting special characteristics of the stress pattern in that language. ... Some of the entries have no descriptive source. These must be handled with caution. The stress pattern in these languages was deduced from old scanty material found in the Australian Institute for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies (AIATSIS) library and at the Australian National University (ANU). It may be that some of them have been mistakenly placed in a certain category, due to missing crucial information. Yet, they were included for completeness sake.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Main stress on the first syllable of the word (Goedemans's survey category II); the placement is Goedemans's own inference from O'Grady's 1957 unpublished fieldnotes, not a statement in a description of Ngarluma. Consistent with von Brandenstein 1967:14, who writes Ngarluma citation forms with an initial stress mark ('kabunkalaragu, 'purakuragu) in contrast to lenited Yindjibarndi forms where stress shifts off the first syllable onto derived long vowels.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly 'no info on sec stress' (category II).
new_statements.exceptions: None; Goedemans flags all 'inferred' entries as possibly misclassified.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level main stress in a typological survey; no phonetic or phrase-level detail. von Brandenstein's supporting marks are on isolated oblique word forms.
new_statements.identity_note: Goedemans's entry is 'Ngarluma (T76)' (Tindale number), i.e. Ngarluma proper = ngar1287; his inference rests on O'Grady's 1957 Pilbara fieldnotes. von Brandenstein's Ngarluma data come from East Ngarluma speakers (Austlang: 'all his informants spoke East Ngarluma'); Austlang W38 also notes that on purely linguistic criteria Kariyarra (W39, Glottolog kari1304) and Ngarluma are dialects of one language, but none of the sources examined here describes Kariyarra.

sources.citation: Hall, Harold Aubrey, with concordance and commentary by C.G. von Brandenstein. 1971. A partial vocabulary of the Ngalooma Aboriginal tribe. Canberra: Australian Institute of Aboriginal Studies. iv+80 pp.
sources.note: von Brandenstein's notes on 'Hall's Orthography' and 'The new Ngarluma Orthography' (pp.77-78) treat consonant series, gemination, vowels and length only; the word 'stress' occurs only in glosses ('a suffix stressing a word'). Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: von Brandenstein, C.G. 1967. The language situation in the Pilbara - past and present. In Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 2, Pacific Linguistics A-11:1-20. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Note 17, p.14: Ngarluma citation forms are transcribed with an initial stress mark ('gabungalaragu / 'kabunkalaragu 'with-foreskin-Obl.', 'buraguragu / 'purakuragu 'cormorant-Obl.') against lenited Jindjiparndi gauna'lau, bu'au, and he remarks 'In normal, i.e. fast, speech only the shift of stress from the first syllable will reveal vowel length'. Implies default first-syllable stress but states no rule for Ngarluma.
